title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a transition between the end of §40 and the opening of §41, in Grothendieck's continuation of the Longue Marche (pagination 315).

(1) End of §40. Grothendieck has derived, in §38, certain 'congruence' relations. These are conditions on exterior (outer) automorphisms of the profinite completion π̂_{0,3}. Here π_{0,3} is the fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, free on the loops ℓ_0, ℓ_1, ℓ_∞ subject to ℓ_0ℓ_1ℓ_∞ = 1. The automorphisms in question are those that could come from Π_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q).

He now asks a methodological question:
- Are these relations genuinely arithmetic, i.e. specific to the outer action coming from Π_Q?
- Or are they more or less automatic consequences of an 'algebraic' formalism of profinite groups, modelled ('calqué') on the discrete case of §40 (cartographic groups, PGL/GL(2) over Z)?

Without prejudging the answer, or how plausible such formalisms are, he proposes to try to extract one experimentally and see where it leads.

(2) Title of §41: 'Condition of commutation of π̂'_{0,3} ≅ Ĝ^+_{0,3} with the operations of Π_Q; computation of exterior automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} and Ĝ^+_{0,3}.'
- Π_Q acts by outer automorphisms on π̂_{0,3}.
- G^+_{0,3} is the oriented triangulated cartographic group, π_{0,3}/⟨⟨ℓ_1^2, ℓ_∞^3⟩⟩ ≅ Z/2 * Z/3 ≅ PSL(2,Z).
- This group is the orbifold fundamental group of the j-line, i.e. of the modular stack M_{1,1} modulo ±1. It is also the quotient of π_{0,3} by the 2- and 3-torsion relations (see the next page).

Before attempting the formalism, he wants to settle a prior question: which further necessary conditions (beyond the §38 congruence conditions) must an outer automorphism of π̂_{0,3} satisfy to come from Π_Q?

The candidate condition is compatibility with the epimorphism φ̂: π̂_{0,3} → Ĝ^+_{0,3}. In modern terms, an element of Out(F̂_2) coming from Galois must:
- preserve the closed normal subgroup generated by ℓ_1^2 and ℓ_∞^3 (with the appropriate inertia conditions);
- hence induce an outer action on PSL(2,Z)^.

This is exactly the kind of condition that leads to the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT̂: the 2-cycle and 3-cycle (hexagon) relations, and the GT action on π̂_1(M_{1,1}).

The overarching problem is the 'arithmetic vs formal' question: is the image of Gal(Q̄/Q) in Out(π̂_{0,3}) cut out by group-theoretic conditions? This is the central question of the anabelian / Grothendieck–Teichmüller programme.
errors: No mathematical claims are made on this page, only questions and a programme, so there is nothing to check for correctness.
Minor: the title's π̂^1_{0,3} is presumably π̂'_{0,3}. The next page defines π'_{0,3} = π_{0,3}/{ℓ_1^2, ℓ_∞^3}.

ideas.what: Question whether congruence-type conditions on outer automorphisms of π̂_{0,3} are specifically arithmetic (Galois) or formal consequences of a profinite group-theoretic formalism modelled on the discrete case.
ideas.modern_name: Is Gal(Q̄/Q) = GT̂? (the problem of characterizing the Galois image in Out(F̂_2) group-theoretically)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984); Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara (1990s) for GT̂
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (the Teichmüller tower and 'formal' description of Gal(Q̄/Q) via Out of profinite fundamental groups); La Longue Marche

ideas.what: Necessary condition for a Galois-type outer automorphism of π̂_{0,3}: compatibility with the epimorphism to the oriented triangulated cartographic group Ĝ^+_{0,3} ≅ PSL(2,Z)^, i.e. preservation of the normal subgroup generated by ℓ_1^2 and ℓ_∞^3.
ideas.modern_name: GT̂ / Galois action on π̂_1(M_{1,1}) and on PSL(2,Z)^; the 2-3 (hexagon) relations
ideas.where_published: Cartographic groups appear in Esquisse d'un programme; this specific commutation condition is unsure

ideas.what: Planned computation of the outer automorphism groups of π̂_{0,3} and Ĝ^+_{0,3}.
ideas.usually_credited_to: various (e.g. Out(PSL2(Z)^) studied in GT literature)

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes to extract, experimentally, a profinite formalism modelled on the discrete cartographic/PGL(2) case, to test whether his §38 congruence relations are automatic (non-arithmetic). The outcome is not on this page. The idea of deriving GT-like relations from a 'discrete-modelled' formalism, rather than from Teichmüller-tower considerations, is a slightly different route from Drinfeld's.
missed.quote: Sans préjuger aucunement la réponse et des degrés de plausibilité de ces telles formalismes, je pourrais à titre expérimental essayer d'en dégager une, pour tester où il en mènera.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical witness that Grothendieck independently formulated, around the Longue Marche, the question of whether profinite group-theoretic conditions (beyond congruence relations) cut out the Galois image. That question is now the GT̂ vs Gal_Q problem. It is of mainly historical interest unless the following pages contain explicit relations.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a transitional and programmatic page. The questions posed (arithmetic vs formal relations; compatibility with the map to PSL(2,Z)^) anticipate the Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory, but they are known to be in Grothendieck's programme (Esquisse). The page contains no explicit new result.
transcription_corrections: '(valable[?] sur le cas discret' should read roughly '({qui serait} calqué sur le cas discret'. The insertion 'qui serait' goes with 'calqué', not with 'formalisme'.
The insertion above 'formalisme' reads 'provenance "algébrique"' (possibly 'provenant "algébriques"'). It qualifies 'conséquences ± automatiques d'un formalisme des groupes profinis'.
In the title, 'Π̂^1_{0,3}' should likely be 'π̂'_{0,3}' (primed), consistent with the next page.
'Autom. extérieurs' is in the title. The struck word 'tentative' is replaced by 'voie', as transcribed.
